newsitem.title: USA: Summit CEO exit may lift company - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Summit CEO exit may lift company - analysts.

text.p: The departure of Summit Technology Chief Executive Officer David Muller may allow the company to work out some of its legal and regulatory problems and re-evaluate its aggressive expansion plans, analysts said.
A pair of government investigations, shareholder lawsuits, losses from its vision-correction centers and lingering skepticism over Summit's technology have hurt its share price.
"I think that David Muller gave a bad image to the company," said Anne Anderson, an analyst with Atlantis Investment. "I think investors are relieved he is leaving."
Summit, which traded as high as 38-3/4 in December, was up 5/16 at 6-1/8 at 1330 EDT/1730 GMT Friday.

Summit announced earlier that its board of directors dismissed Muller as chairman and chief executive, and appointed the company's president, Verne Sharma, as chair of an executive committee and interim CEO.

In April, Summit said Muller, who founded the laser eye correction company a decade ago, received in late 1995 a package of what appeared to be internal U.S. Food and Drug Administration documents on a laser eye system under development by arch-rival VISX Inc. Summit said the FDA was conducting an internal investigation.
